as_told.title: Space mission patches with opaque Latin mottos

plain: A religious studies professor named Diana Pasulka tells podcast host Jesse Michels that people in the space world told her the Latin symbols on their mission patches, the cloth badges made for each launch, were a way to pay homage to beings they call the sponsors. She says that when she asked whether the sponsors read Latin, they said absolutely, though elsewhere in the same talk she places the patches in today's Space Force without the sponsors claim. If true, it would mean some people in the space programme believe they answer to non-human patrons.
